content.title: About
content.content: Tortilla chips are crunchy slices made from corn tortillas that are fried or baked until golden. The Doritos line offers a wide range of flavors, from classic cheese to spicy and aromatic blends such as chili‑lime, taco, and barbecue.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial Doritos brand was launched in the United States in 1966 by Frito‑Lay.
In 1972 the iconic "Nacho Cheese" flavor was introduced and became the best‑selling variety worldwide.
There are more than 30 permanent Doritos flavors, plus seasonal limited‑edition releases.
Tortilla chips are made from whole‑grain corn, making them naturally gluten‑free.
In some markets Doritos are sold as "stacks" – thicker, softer pieces rather than traditional chips.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Corn chips provide carbohydrates that quickly supply the body with energy, making them a convenient snack before physical activity.

items.title: Contains fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain corn contributes a modest amount of dietary fiber, supporting digestive health.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Certain flavors, such as tomato or pepper blends, contain natural antioxidants from spices.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Made from pure corn, tortilla chips are suitable for people with gluten intolerance.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Corn provides thiamine, niacin, and folate, which play roles in metabolism.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Many Doritos flavors contain a notable amount of salt, which can raise blood pressure if consumed frequently.

items.title: Fat and calorie density
items.content: Fried chips are high in fats and calories, so they should be eaten in moderation, especially for weight management.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Some varieties contain dairy, soy, or spice ingredients that may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Products made with partially hydrogenated oils may contain trans fats, which are detrimental to heart health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tortilla chips are perfect as a standalone snack, tossed into salads, paired with guacamole or salsa, or used as a base for loaded nachos. They pair well with cheese, beans, vegetables, and a variety of dips.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep chips in the original package or an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, store them in the refrigerator to maintain crunchiness and prevent fat oxidation.
